payload.title: Reprice trusts ledger-controlled resolved_model hints for otherwise unresolvable models
payload.description: `reprice_row` falls back from an unresolvable `model` to `row.get("resolved_model")` and then marks the row as `pricing_source: "config"`. Because `resolved_model` is read from the historical ledger row itself, a malformed or attacker-influenced ledger entry can be converted into a trusted priced row for a different catalog model without proving that the original provider/model maps to that catalog entry. That can understate or overstate historical costs and reduce `unpriced_rows`, affecting budget-certification logic after an operator runs `cost-report.sh --reprice`.
payload.recommendation: Do not use ledger-supplied `resolved_model` as a pricing authority for unresolved models. Only reprice via `find_pricing(provider, model, config)` or a config-owned alias/hop mapping. If legacy rows need hints, validate the hint against an auditable config mapping or mark those rows as still unpriced.
